Doctor. Good morning, Mr. Sharma. Please, have a seat. What brings you in today? Patient. Good morning, doctor. Thank you. For the past three or four days, I've been having some trouble with my right eye. It feels quite dry, it gets red by the end of the day, and my vision gets a bit blurry when I'm working on my laptop. Doctor. I see. Are you experiencing any pain, discharge, or sensitivity to light? Patient.
No severe pain, just a mild gritty sensation, like there's a grain of sand stuck in it. No discharge, but my eye waters occasionally when I strain. Doctor. All right. How many hours a day do you typically spend looking at screens? Patient. Quite a bit, actually. Around eight to ten hours a day for work, plus using my phone in the evening. Doctor. That's very common. Let's do a quick physical examination first.
We'll check your vision using the eye chart and take a look at the front of your eye using the slit lamp microscope. The doctor conducts the visual acuity test and examines the patient's eyes with the slit lamp. Doctor. Everything structurally looks healthy. Your retina and intraocular pressure are normal, and there's no sign of infection. What you're experiencing is classic digital eye strain combined with dry eye syndrome.
Patient. Ah, that makes sense. I definitely forget to take breaks. Is it reversible, doctor? Doctor. Absolutely. Here is what we'll do. Lubricating eye drops. I'm prescribing preservative-free artificial tears. Use one drop in each eye three to four times a day to keep your eyes clean. Patient.
Patient. Patient. Patient. Patient. Patient. Patient.
Patient. Patient. Patient.
